title: Decode coded variables to plain text (and vice versa)
text: main purpose packgae twofold: easily translate coded variables plain text using standardised dictionaries. provide infrastructure create dictionaries. first purpose assumed dominate package therefore includes several dictionaries compatible data INCA Rockan.

title: Decode coded variables to plain text (and vice versa)
text: Assume dataset (less) typical RCC-data:
code: set.seed(12345) n <- 6 s <- function(x) sample(x, n, replace = TRUE)  incadata <-    data.frame(     KON_VALUE = s(1:2),     region = 1:6,     a_icdo3 = c("C446", "C749", "C159", "C709", "C475", "C320"),     a_tstad = c("0", "1", "1a", "1b", "1c", "2")   ) knitr::kable(incadata)

title: Decode coded variables to plain text (and vice versa)
text: decode generic S3-function accepts R-object different kinds. default method takes atomic vector codes specification translate codes (see ?decode). See ?key_value_data list available keyvalue objects included package.
code: library(decoder)  decode(incadata$KON_VALUE, "kon") ## [1] "Kvinna" "Man"    "Kvinna" "Kvinna" "Kvinna" "Kvinna" decode(incadata$a_tstad, "t_rtr") ## [1] "T0"  "T1"  "T1a" "T1b" "T1c" "T2"

title: Decode coded variables to plain text (and vice versa)
text: far, looked cases code can littaraly translated keyvalue object. however third argument decode function, exact, FALSE default. often useful allow automatic transformation variables know coded values exactly keyvalue object. common application probably want extract municipality names LKF-variable. can obviosly done : also possible use original six digit code : Note last value decodes NA cases. preffered original codes stored character, since preserves leading 0 “048005”: can also taken care reading data use_incadata function (see ?incadata::use_incadata), always classifies numbers leading zeros characters (numeric) (covered vignette). Note use exact = FALSE (default convenience) always produce warnings transformations done. always recommended manually confirm transformations fact accurate. Unexpected results might otherwise occur!
code: x <- c(178405, 138408, 108202, 128706, 048005) y <- as.numeric(substring(as.character(x), 1, 4)) decode(y, "kommun", exact = TRUE) ## Warning: Some codes could not be translated (4800) ## [1] "Arvika"     "Kungsbacka" "Karlshamn"  "Trelleborg" NA decode(x, "kommun") ## Warning: transformed to match the keyvalue: Only the first 4 characters are ## used. ## Warning: Some codes could not be translated (48005) ## [1] "Arvika"     "Kungsbacka" "Karlshamn"  "Trelleborg" NA decode("048005", "kommun") ## Warning: transformed to match the keyvalue: Only the first 4 characters are ## used. ## [1] "Nyköping"

title: Decode coded variables to plain text (and vice versa)
text: atomic vector method additional argument extra_functions can used modify outcome decoded variable. Read man page (?decode) details complete list available extra functions. default regional names used INCA used default “region” keyvalue: Sometimes however convenient use abbriviated form names : also achieved additional keyvalue object containing hard coded short names additional advantage “extra_function” method several extra functions can chained:
code: decode(1:6, "region") ## [1] "Region Sthlm/Gotland"  "Region Uppsala/Örebro" "Region Sydöstra"       ## [4] "Region Syd"            "Region Väst"           "Region Norr" decode(1:6, "region", "short_region_names") ## [1] "Sthlm/Gotland"  "Uppsala/Örebro" "Sydöstra"       "Syd"            ## [5] "Väst"           "Norr" munic_west <- c("1382", "1419", "1441", "1460", "1472", "1488", "1496") decode(munic_west, "sjukvardsomrade", c("kungalv2Storgoteborg", "real_names")) ## [1] "Norra Halland"  "Storgöteborg"   "Södra Älvsborg" "Fyrbodal"       ## [5] "Skaraborg"      "Fyrbodal"       "Skaraborg"

title: Decode coded variables to plain text (and vice versa)
text: simplest situation (1:1 relation code value), code just inverse decode: decode however also allow translation m:1 dictionaries snomed (gives differnt result snomed3): decoding can inverted: restriction applies requested values de facto non unique. tied keyvalue object .
code: code(c("Karlskrona", "Göteborg", "Härnösand"), "kommun") ## [1] "1080" "1480" "2280" non_unique <- c(90703, 90723, 96153, 99403, 89643, 90443) decode(non_unique, "snomed") ## [1] "Embryonalt carcinom" "Embryonalt carcinom" "Hårcellsleukemi"     ## [4] "Hårcellsleukemi"     "Klarcellssarkom"     "Klarcellssarkom" code(decode(non_unique, "snomed"), "snomed") ##       key               value ## 393 90703 Embryonalt carcinom ## 402 90723 Embryonalt carcinom ## 592 96153     Hårcellsleukemi ## 787 99403     Hårcellsleukemi ## 354 89643     Klarcellssarkom ## 381 90443     Klarcellssarkom ## Error in `code()`: ## ! Values above have a non unique relation to their key! unique <- c(   "Mucinöst kystadenom (kystom) borderline-typ ( 2 B)",    "Medullärt carcinom, atypiskt",    "Mb Paget non invasiv och intraduktal",    "Lymfangiosarcom, misst",    "Fibröst histiocytom, malignt",    "Ganglioneurom",    "Carcinoid (exkl appendix)",    "Langerhans cell histiocytos, UNS, Histiocytosis X, UNS",    "Brenner tumör, malign",    "Lymfatisk leukemi, UNS") code(unique, "snomed") ##  [1] "84723" "85133" "85432" "91701" "88303" "94900" "82403" "97511" "90003" ## [10] "98203"
